results.correct_value: Camping within Snowgrass Flat is prohibited; the approach must not recommend camping in the flat. The itinerary's higher camp (~7,100-7,200 ft, above the flat) is unaffected.
results.evidence: The Gifford Pinchot wilderness regulations prohibit camping within Snowgrass Flat and Shoe Lake Basin; a trail guide repeats that camping at Snowgrass Flat is prohibited and places the lower portion of the flat at the Lily Basin junction (4.1 mi). A trip report camped near 7,200 ft above the basin, consistent with the itinerary. Approach, approach variant and the Lily Basin junction waypoint note no longer present the flat as a camp. The waypoint's type is still 'Campsite' (type not patched) and bivy is out of scope.

results.evidence: One trip report gives 14.2 mi round trip for the two-summit trip (matching totalNote) and a camp near 7,200 ft, but no source gives the trailhead-to-camp or camp-to-trailhead distance, so the 7 mi in vs 6.5 mi out vs summit-at-7-mi cannot be settled.

The schedule (5:30 AM to ~4:30-5 PM) implies ~11 h against 8 h in the day and timing. One trip report took 7.3 h for the Old Snowy/Ives loop from camp alone, which supports a longer day than 8 h with the hike-out, but no two sources state the day length, and changing it would cascade into timing.totalHrs.

One trip report gives ~2,400 ft for the Old Snowy/Ives loop from a lower camp; the stored 900 ft looks too low, but the itinerary total (2,500+900) equals gain_ft 3,400 and no source states this route's car-to-car gain for the two-summit plan, so per the rules no day figure is changed.

results.correct_value: Goat Creek is crossed on a footbridge just before the 2-mile mark (not a ford).
results.evidence: One trail guide says a sturdy bridge crosses Goat Creek just before 2 mi; another says a sturdy footbridge at 1.9 mi; a trip report also records the Goat Creek bridge crossing under two miles.

results.correct_value: No crevassed glacier travel, but the McCall Glacier's moat or edge near the Old Snowy-Ives col may have to be crossed early in the season.
results.evidence: A trip report traversed steep snow and a narrow moat of the McCall Glacier on the way to Ives; a route description says the boot path from Old Snowy toward Ives runs until the McCall Glacier blocks it, with the moat, the glacier edge or dropping south as options. The crevasses line was reworded so it no longer says 'N/A' against the hazards and watch-out entries (and no longer calls the route 'NE Slopes').
